body: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Webhell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Webhell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Webhell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.
summaryZh: 本文提出了Webhell，一种用于智能体网页访问的统一接口框架。针对现有网页访问模型在信息收集与交互操作之间的割裂问题，Webhell通过WebContract定义通用模式，将网页内容编译为可寻址的对象，并利用WebCache进行持久化管理。这种设计使得智能体能够更高效地执行长程任务。实验证明，Webhell在网页搜索、导航及深度研究任务中均表现出更优的性能与成本效益，强调了接口设计对提升智能体网页交互能力的重要性。
